summary:
Every day, NASA satellites beam petabytes of Earth observation data to humanity, yet climate awareness remains abstract because statistics like "1.5°C anomaly" or "426 PPM CO₂" feel detached from daily human experience.

As a solo developer, I built GAIA — an intelligent, high-fidelity planetary digital twin that gives Earth an embodied voice. Grounded in empirical NASA satellite telemetry (Terra/Aqua MODIS Land Surface Temperature), USGS elevation data, and NOAA atmospheric series, GAIA transforms planetary observation into an intimate, interactive conversation.

By combining stationary WebGL rendering for 100% precision sub-millimeter UV raycasting, custom GLSL thermodynamic heat shaders with binary landmasking, neural speech synthesis, real-time celestial mechanics (Sun, Moon, ISS, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Venus), and a mobile-adaptive device engine, I designed GAIA so anyone can tap anywhere on Earth and listen to the living story of their planet.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

GAIA embodies planet Earth as an interactive digital twin that humans can converse with:

  • Stationary Earth with Exact UV Raycasting: Earth is stationary by default to ensure 100% click precision. Clicking any coordinate calculates latitude and longitude via spherical UV projection: phi = (0.5 - v) * 180°, theta = (u - 0.5) * 360°, reverse-geocodes the exact city or marine basin, and triggers localized telemetry.
  • MODIS Land-Only Thermal LST Shader: Uses a 2048x1024 binary land-sea mask to ensure thermodynamic heat dome anomalies render strictly on continental land masses, leaving ocean basins unpolluted.
  • Chronos Timeline Engine: Users can scrub from the Year 2000 through 2026 (Present Day) to 2050 (IPCC Climate Projection) with dynamic temperature and CO₂ shifts, or activate 1-click animated time-lapse.
  • Solar System & Orbital Context: Features 7 interactable celestial bodies (Sun with solar flare corona, Moon with tidal locking, ISS with 51.6° orbital inclination, Mars, Jupiter with 4 Galilean moons, Saturn with nested rings and Cassini Division, and Venus).
  • Universal Device Recognition Engine: Adapts dynamically across Mobile, Tablet, and Desktop with a touch drag vs. tap discriminator and a collapsible mobile voice pill.

What Benefits & Impact Does It Have?

  • Scientific Empathy: Replaces passive charts with an embodied planetary persona, turning climate apathy into scientific engagement.
  • Universal Accessibility: Fully responsive on mobile smartphones without requiring app store installation or high-end GPU workstations (DPR is capped at 1.75 to preserve mobile battery and thermals).

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software

  • Languages: JavaScript (ES6+), GLSL (OpenGL Shading Language), Python 3.12, HTML5, CSS3.
  • Libraries & Frameworks: Three.js, GSAP 3.12, Tailwind CSS, Flask, HTTPX, Edge-TTS, Pillow.
  • Datasets: NASA MODIS (MOD11A2), NASA Blue Marble, USGS GMTED2010, NOAA Mauna Loa Keeling Curve, NASA JPL Horizons.

How Is Your Project Creative?

Instead of building another dashboard of charts, GAIA reimagines the planet as a living entity. Every celestial body (Sun, Moon, ISS, Saturn) has its own voice and physically grounded astronomical behaviors. All planetary textures for celestial bodies are generated dynamically through pure algorithmic canvas mathematics rather than static images.

Factors Considered (Solo Developer Perspective)

As a solo developer, I prioritized three core factors:

  1. Zero-Lag Mobile Responsiveness: Ensuring the full 3D simulation runs at 60 FPS on mobile phones through touch gesture discrimination.
  2. Scientific Rigor: Keeping terrestrial heat anomalies strictly on land using binary raster masking.
  3. Turnkey Execution: Creating 1-click local startup scripts (run_gaia.bat and run_gaia.sh) for judges to test instantly.
